query: For a CoCrFeNi high-entropy-alloy matrix evaluated in sliding from room temperature to 800 °C, what single intervention could overcome the difficulty of maintaining low coefficient of friction and wear rate throughout the full temperature range? Earlier studies of other self-lubricating material systems reported low coefficients of friction at 704 °C and favorable friction and wear behavior over broad temperature ranges. However, these results do not resolve the limited understanding of wide-temperature tribological performance in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys, and effectiveness must be maintained as operating temperature, load, and environment vary. Formulate one hypothesis that identifies a single intervention without presupposing its class, explains its mechanism, predicts friction and wear relative to the starting CoCrFeNi material, defines its temperature, load, and environmental boundaries, relates it to prior evidence, and specifies a controlled experiment with a clear result that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a high‐temperature stable self-lubricating surface treatment to CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys will form an in situ lubricious tribolayer that reduces friction and wear consistently from room temperature to 800 °C compared to the untreated alloy.
generation.material_initial_state: CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloy matrix without any surface modification.
generation.intervention: A single, controlled surface treatment that deposits a high-temperature stable, self-lubricating coating onto the alloy substrate.
generation.conditions: Sliding tests conducted under controlled loads in an air atmosphere over a temperature range from ~25 °C to 800 °C.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation and retention of a shearable and oxidation-resistant lubricious tribolayer derived from the coating that mitigates direct metal-to-metal contact during sliding.
generation.mechanism: The coating is designed to form a stable, low-shear interface even as temperature rises, thereby preventing excessive friction and wear. Its oxidation-resistant properties enable the tribolayer to remain intact in environments where the untreated alloy would otherwise suffer degradation.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to the baseline, the coated samples will exhibit a more uniform and reduced coefficient of friction and lower wear rates across the entire temperature range, with particularly enhanced performance at higher temperatures (700 °C to 800 °C).
generation.baseline: Untreated CoCrFeNi alloy, which shows variable friction and increased wear, especially under high-temperature sliding conditions.
generation.boundary: The improved performance is expected under the tested conditions (moderate loads, air environment, and temperatures from ~25 °C to 800 °C). Performance in highly aggressive environments or at loads well beyond the testing regime may deviate from these predictions.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal formulation and structure of the coating are not fully established, and its long-term adhesion and durability under cyclic thermal stress remain to be validated. The exact magnitude of friction and wear improvements is also uncertain.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of CoCrFeNi samples: one set receives the self-lubricating coating and the other remains untreated. Subject both sets to identical sliding tribometer tests where temperature is ramped gradually from room temperature to 800 °C under controlled load and air atmosphere conditions. Conduct surface analyses post-testing to verify tribolayer formation.
measurements: Continuous measurement of the coefficient of friction throughout the temperature ramp
Wear rate determination (e.g., mass loss or volume loss) post-test
Surface characterization (SEM, XPS) to assess the presence and stability of the lubricious tribolayer
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the coated samples do not show a statistically significant decrease in friction coefficient and wear rate across the temperature range, or if the tribolayer is not present or degrades during the test, the hypothesis will be falsified.
